prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: Company news: retail, restaurant, apparel, travel and leisure.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Every material company-specific news item for US-listed retail, restaurant, apparel, travel and leisure companies >= $1B in the window, as many as you can find: press releases, 8-K filings, executive changes, activist campaigns, legal settlements, contracts, product launches, guidance, analyst rating/PT changes (firm, old → new), and the stock move. One bullet per company.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **WMT** — Retail
- Deutsche Bank upgraded Walmart to **Buy from Hold** and raised its price target to **$136 from $113**; shares were up approximately **2.2% premarket** and around **2% during Thursday trading** (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15 07:19 ET; Investopedia, Oct. 15, time not stated).[4][3]

## **NFLX** — Entertainment / Leisure
- Jefferies initiated coverage with a **Buy** rating and an **$85 price target**; shares were up approximately **0.7% premarket** (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15 07:19 ET).[4]

## **TNL** — Travel & Leisure
- Susquehanna lowered its price target to **$75 from $95** while maintaining a **Positive** rating; shares opened at **$62.61** and were down **0.6%** Thursday (MarketBeat/Benzinga, Oct. 15, time not stated).[5]

## **TXRH** — Restaurants
- Stephens upgraded Texas Roadhouse to **Overweight from Equal Weight** and kept its price target at **$205** (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15 10:39 ET).[10]

## **KMX** — Automotive Retail
- Bank of America upgraded CarMax to **Buy from Underperform** and raised its price target to **$65 from $50** (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15 10:39 ET).[10]

## **ACI** — Grocery Retail
- JPMorgan downgraded Albertsons to **Neutral from Overweight** with a **$14** price target; Goldman Sachs downgraded the stock to **Neutral from Buy** and cut its target to **$13 from $16** following the fiscal second-quarter report (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15 10:39 ET).[10]

## Retail / Apparel Sector
- Nike, Lululemon, Boot Barn, Macy’s and Dick’s Sporting Goods each rose approximately **5%** during Thursday trading, while the SPDR S&P Retail ETF gained more than **3%**; Nike shares ultimately gained approximately **6%** (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, time not stated; Investopedia, Oct. 15, time not stated).[1][3]
